name: QWEN-W4-PREFILL-ROOFLINE-0
note: Machine-readable form of PRE-REG QWEN-W4-PREFILL-ROOFLINE-0; the prose governs on any conflict. Artin's GO (2026-10-25): an architecture-level, measurement-based study of the W4 prefill wall on the PROMOTED generation-5 serving path (the Metal GatedDeltaNet recurrence kernel as the default since VERDICT QWEN-GDN-PROMOTE-0, chunk 256, decode-once float32 GEMM, final-position head, 2 GiB allocator-cache limit), assessment and bounded measurement only: no serving-kernel replacement, no default change, no census. The bars are PREDICTIONS of a performance model, not promotion hurdles: FIRE confirms the model's premise, NO-FIRE refutes it, and nothing is promoted either way. Stage decomp repeats the QWEN-PREFILL-WALL-0 marginal decomposition on the promoted path at the 1,024-token development prompt (never a held-out prompt) with the W4 family split in situ into its decode (slab write, decode kernel, allocation) and its float32 GEMM; stage micro measures on the two real W4 shapes at T = 256, 512 and 1,024 the production decode kernel, the plain fill of the same slab, the float32 GEMM alone, the production decode-then-matmul, the same with the pool cleared, float16 and bfloat16 GEMMs, and mx.quantized_matmul (affine 4-bit, group 128) as the LIBRARY fused dequant-GEMM reference, against the achievable square-GEMM and streaming rates measured in the same process. Candidate rule (registered now, applied after the measurements, every term a named receipt field): w4_share = decomp.marginal.no_w4_mlp.marginal_pct_of_full / 100; decode_share = decomp.w4_split.decode_share_of_w4 and matmul_share = decomp.w4_split.matmul_share_of_w4, both divided by decomp.w4_split.split_sum_over_w4 so they sum to one; the micro terms are the T = 256 rows of micro.matrices for layers.0.mlp.gate_proj and layers.0.mlp.down_proj, count-weighted 128:64 wherever one number is needed. Ceilings as fractions of TTFT: A fused dequant-GEMM, two terms reported separately, A1 = w4_share x decode_share (decode removal at a fixed float32 GEMM, the in-situ no_w4_decode marginal) and A2 = w4_share x (1 - count-weighted library_qmm_affine4_f32_s over production_decode_then_matmul_s) (what the framework's own fused affine kernel demonstrates, which on down_proj also includes a better GEMM schedule than the float32 matmul); B float16 decode and float16 GEMM, B = w4_share x (1 - decode_share x r16 - matmul_share x f16_over_f32), r16 = 0.5 x fill_same_slab_s / single_s (a float16 decode kernel is unmeasured; half the measured write floor is its optimistic proxy), f16_over_f32 count-weighted; B changes the SERVED WEIGHTS (the float16 copies of the W4 weights are inexact, smoke fp16_weights_exact False on both shapes) as well as the activations and the accumulation, so it is a timing ceiling only and any adoption would need its own parity pre-reg; C decoded-weight caching across chunks, C = w4_share x decode_share x (k - 1) / k for k chunks, feasible only if roofline.decoded_slab_cache_resident_gb fits the device's recommended working set (expected infeasible at 68 GB float32 and 34 GB float16 against 30 GB); D chunk 512, D = w4_share x (1 - count-weighted production_decode_then_matmul_s at T = 512 over twice the T = 256 value), cross-checked against the 5 percent VERDICT QWEN-PREFILL-WALL-0 measured on the loop path (a stale transport: the same absolute saving is a larger share of the shorter promoted wall), no new in-situ measurement. AT MOST ONE additional microbenchmark may follow under this GO: the feasible candidate with the largest ceiling whose mechanism the library or dtype measurements demonstrate (for A, A2 at or above 0.10; for B, B at or above 0.10 with the weight inexactness disclosed), and only then under its OWN pre-registration written before any code (timing plus oracle parity against the float32 decode_f32 product on the two shapes, never wired into serving); otherwise no kernel prototype is written and the assessment reports the ceilings. The smoke pipeline run at 256 tokens and T = 64 was seen before registration (disclosed in the prose); the registered values below were fixed from the QWEN-PREFILL-WALL-0 and QWEN-METAL-PREFILL-GEMM-0 receipts, not from the smoke.

PROMOTED.description: the promoted default serving path: llmopt.lab.qserve.Engine() with no arguments (the Metal recurrence kernel selected by name on all 48 DeltaNet layers, generation 5, chunk 256, GEMM scope, 2 GiB cache limit), measured in one process on one Mac; every stand-in is installed and removed inside that process

bars.name: W4-SHARE
bars.description: the W4 MLP family's marginal cost (full minus the path with every W4 linear replaced by a constant, medians of 4 order-balanced runs each) is at least 60 percent of the promoted 1,024-token prefill wall (the earlier study read 48 percent of a wall that still carried the Python recurrence; 12.6 of the projected 17.6 s is 71). Under the 3-point fence a reading between 57 and 63 is UNRESOLVED.

bars.name: DECODE-SHARE
bars.description: the in-situ decode share of the W4 family (the no_w4_decode marginal, which removes the decode kernel, its slab write and its allocation while keeping the float32 GEMM and its slab read against pre-decoded slabs, over the W4 marginal) is under 0.35: the float32 GEMM, not the decode, is the larger part (the per-matrix microbenchmark of QWEN-METAL-PREFILL-GEMM-0 read 3.6 of 14.9 ms, 0.24). This is decode removal at a fixed float32 GEMM, not a fused dequant-GEMM ceiling. Between 0.32 and 0.38 UNRESOLVED.

bars.name: GEMM-EFFICIENCY
bars.description: the float32 GEMM alone at T = 256 on the pre-decoded slab runs within 0.60 of the float32 rate of a 4,096-square matmul measured in the same process, on both W4 shapes (worst of the two: the earlier kernel study read 4.05 TFLOPS on gate_proj and 2.75 on down_proj at T = 256, logs/qmetal/prefill_kernels_7f464353.json, with no square-peak reading of its own; the smoke's 2,048-square read 3.80): the remaining GEMM-schedule headroom at the float32 dtype is bounded by this ratio on each shape. Between 0.57 and 0.63 UNRESOLVED. Note the single-call timing here adds one synchronisation per call where the prior was pipelined.

bars.name: DECODE-BANDWIDTH
bars.description: the production decode kernel moves its bytes (the float32 slab written plus the payload read) at a rate at least 0.60 of the streaming add measured over 1 GiB in the same process, on both shapes (worst of the two): the decode is a bandwidth-bound slab write, not an index or codebook-lookup problem. Between 0.55 and 0.65 UNRESOLVED.

bars.name: LIBRARY-FUSED
bars.description: the framework's own fused in-tile dequantizing GEMM (mx.quantized_matmul, affine 4-bit group 128, FLOAT32 activations, a different codec at about twice the house payload's bits per weight, timing only) at T = 256 takes at least 0.50 of the production decode-then-matmul time on both shapes (worst case over the two shapes; the earlier kernel study read 12.2 against 15.0 ms on gate_proj and 12.6 against 20.7 on down_proj, 0.81 and 0.61, pipelined): a fused dequant-GEMM in this framework saves at most half of the W4 matrix time on either shape. On down_proj the library ratio mixes the fused-decode saving with a better GEMM schedule than the float32 matmul (qmm 12.6 against the matmul alone 16.6). The float16-activation variant is reported descriptively (no prior). Between 0.45 and 0.55 UNRESOLVED. Single-call timing here, pipelined in the prior.

bars.name: ALLOCATION
bars.description: the production decode-then-matmul at T = 256 with the allocator pool cleared before every call (one fresh 356 MB slab allocation, page provisioning included) is at most 1.05 of the warm-pool time on both shapes (worst of the two): ONE slab's allocation is not a limiting factor of an isolated matrix call. Between 1.03 and 1.07 UNRESOLVED. This bar covers the isolated single-slab case only; several slabs live at once (the serving condition inside a chunk under the 2 GiB limit) is reported descriptively through the pipelined-2 and pipelined-4 decode rows (pipelined4_over_single; the smoke read 1.86 on gate_proj) and is inside the in-situ decode marginal of bar 2.

bars.name: GPU-SIDE
bars.description: in one instrumented 1,024-token prefill on the promoted path, GPU completion (complete minus issue, summed over chunks) is at least 0.95 of the wall: the CPU issue and the host-side embedding decode are under 5 percent (the earlier study measured 98 percent with the Python recurrence present; the smoke 0.998). This term lumps GPU work, synchronisation waits and allocation together; the separation of allocation and synchronisation comes from the micro stage and the serialisation penalty of the additive run, not from this bar. Between 0.94 and 0.96 UNRESOLVED.

bars.name: SPLIT-ADDS
bars.description: the two W4 sub-marginals (decode, matmul) sum to between 0.85 and 1.15 of the W4 family marginal: the split is a valid partition (little overlap between the decode and the GEMM in the pipelined path, as the per-matrix microbenchmark read production at 1.0 of the sum of its parts). Outside the band the split is reported as overlapping and bar 2 is read with that caveat.

refuted_if: the performance model's premise (the W4 matrix family is the dominant term of the promoted prefill and its float32 GEMM, not its decode, is the larger part of that family) is refuted if bar 1 or bar 2 reads NO-FIRE; the structured predicate covers bar 1 only, the prose governs.
registered_prior: From VERDICT QWEN-PREFILL-WALL-0 (loop path, 1,017 tokens): W4 MLP 12.6 s marginal of 26.2, DeltaNet recurrence 9.0, S16 body 5.2, rest under 1 s; removing the recurrence projects 17.6 s against the measured 18.1 on the kernel path, so W4 is expected near 70 percent. From QWEN-METAL-PREFILL-GEMM-0 (logs/qmetal/prefill_gemm/bench_9c427901.json): at T = 256 one 17408 x 5120 W4 matrix costs 14.9 ms on the GEMM path, 3.6 ms of it the decode and 11.6 the float32 matmul, so the decode share is expected near 0.24 and the sum of parts near 1.0 of production. From OBSERVATION QWEN-METAL-PREFILL-STUDY-0 (logs/qmetal/prefill_kernels_7f464353.json, T = 256, pipelined): gate_proj float32 matmul 11.3 ms at 4.05 TFLOPS, float16 10.0, framework affine-4 qmm 12.2, decode plus matmul 15.0; down_proj float32 matmul 16.6 ms at 2.75 TFLOPS, qmm 12.6, decode plus matmul 20.7; so the GEMM efficiency differs by shape (expected 0.65 to 0.95 of a square peak near 4.2 TFLOPS) and the library fused reference is expected between 0.5 and 0.8 of production. float16 matmul 0.89 of float32 at 3.5e-4 relative error (QWEN-PREFILL-WALL-0 design receipt). Expected Amdahl ceilings: A (perfect fused dequant-GEMM) about 0.70 x 0.24 = 17 percent of TTFT at best, realistically what the library reference shows; B (float16) about 14 percent with changed numerics; C infeasible (68 GB float32, 34 GB float16 of decoded slabs against a 30 GB working set); D 5 percent. Expected outcome: every bar FIRE, candidates A and B near or above the 0.10 line, and no serving change recommended from this study alone.
